To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the standard model is an excellent low energy effective theory for the description of the strong and electroweak interactions of the quarks and leptons, that the chiral expansion of the standard model is well behaved, and that the chiral perturbation theory is an extremely useful tool in the study of the low energy phenomenology of the standard model.

the low energy constants (LECs) of chiral perturbation theory (ChPT) can be determined with good accuracy from experimental data and that ChPT can be used to extract from data the fundamental parameters of the standard model (SM) with a precision that is comparable with that of the lattice QCD approach.

(1) the standard model of particle physics, with the inclusion of the Higgs field and the Higgs particle, provides a consistent and coherent theoretical framework to describe the observed particle physics phenomena; and (2) the standard model is an incomplete theory, and the observed phenomena are consistent with the existence of new physics beyond the standard model, but the new physics has not yet been observed.
